### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/formula`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **15** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/formula/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**17** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 45bec43cd981684906a0b4c1a8e15d08ca9ec09f`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/formula/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **144** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 45bec43cd981684906a0b4c1a8e15d08ca9ec09f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `906cfd34faeab16fdd879006996b1382800b69cb` — the merge of head `1a3f686027301ca2d066a6f83ffff0b9e6a49f7d` into base `45bec43cd981684906a0b4c1a8e15d08ca9ec09f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 906cfd34faeab16fdd879006996b1382800b69cb && git checkout 906cfd34faeab16fdd879006996b1382800b69cb
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 45bec43cd981684906a0b4c1a8e15d08ca9ec09f 1a3f686027301ca2d066a6f83ffff0b9e6a49f7d && git checkout -B drift-repro 45bec43cd981684906a0b4c1a8e15d08ca9ec09f && git merge --no-ff 1a3f686027301ca2d066a6f83ffff0b9e6a49f7d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 45bec43cd981684906a0b4c1a8e15d08ca9ec09f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 45bec43cd981684906a0b4c1a8e15d08ca9ec09f` → pass the list as

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d347ecd105c81d7aed9b6cc7e5b2d7af80fbff3a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ui/page.zod.ts, packages/formula/src/stdlib.ts, packages/formula/src/types.ts, packages/formula/src/cel-engine.ts, packages/formula/src/index.ts, packages/formula/src/capability-predicate.test.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-visibility-predicates.test.ts, content/docs/references/ui/page.mdx, .changeset/24414-capability-predicate.md + packages/formula/src/unknown-function.ts, packages/formula/src/eval-permissions.ts, packages/formula/src/permission-predicate.test.ts, packages/formula/src/cel-stdlib-drift.test.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-visibility-predicates.ts, packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts, packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts, packages/core/src/security/assemble-execution-context.ts, packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/current-user-endpoints.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/default-permission-sets.ts, packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/execution-context.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/security/permission.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/identity/eval-user.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/app.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts, docs/adr/0066-unified-authorization-model.md, docs/adr/0068-unified-user-context-and-built-in-identity-roles.md, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs, and in the sibling objectui checkout at 2ec9e2a: packages/react/src/hooks/useCapabilityGate.ts, packages/app-shell/src/providers/expressionUser.ts

Base read against: `git merge-base origin/main pr/24478` = `ec951e29e451863295afdd74e1a49e05b2ff281a`. Head check-runs: 41 completed, 36 success, 5 skipped (Console Pin Gate, Dogfood shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke, Temporal Conformance), 0 failed; the five required contexts (Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core, Build Core, Governed Surface Queue Guard) are all `success`. No path of the diff is a `GOVERNED_SURFACES` row. Head repo = base repo (not a fork). The PR is draft, auto-merge unarmed.

### ① Derived judgments

**The predicate `current_user.hasCapability(name)` — accept set, judged right.**
- Receiver-only: registered as `dyn.hasCapability(dyn): bool` (`registerCapabilityPredicate`, `stdlib.ts`), the same form `can` takes; a bare call faults in cel-js as a call-form fault, pinned (`capability-predicate.test.ts` "a bare hasCapability(name) names no subject"). Right: one subject-binding mechanism for both permission predicates, identity-checked (`receiver !== binding.subject` throws).
- Held → true, not held → false, empty list → false: `held.includes(name)` over the bound list; pinned in both directions and for the empty list.
- Absent list → throws; off-shape list → throws; wrong receiver → throws; non-string or empty name → throws; all reported as `ok: false, kind: 'runtime'`. Pinned per arm, each pin asserting the fault message and `ok === false` (never a quiet `false`).
- No registry lookup: the body consults nothing but `binding.systemPermissions`; pinned with an undeclared name answered true when held and false when not.
- **"Empty → false beside absent → throws" is right.** It is `can`'s own pair (empty map → false, absent map → throws, `permission-predicate.test.ts:132/146`), and it is the published list's own semantics: `/auth/me/permissions` serves `systemPermissions: []` as the closed "holds nothing" answer and OMITS the key only on the deliberate degraded branch where the server enforces nothing (`current-user-endpoints.ts` `closedMePermissionsGrants`, `mePermissionsBody`); objectui's `useCapabilityGate` reads an absent array as unknown (fail open) and an empty array as "holds nothing". The predicate's two-valued treatment of the same two states is the honest mirror; the one difference — the predicate THROWS where the client gate fails open — lands the viewer in the same place (a faulting page predicate renders the component), and the describe says so.
- **Same data, same normalisation, same aliases as the action gate — verified, with two structural residuals named.** The server gate is `actionPermissionError` (`packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts:677`): `new Set(ec.systemPermissions ?? [])`, `required.filter(p =` not in set`)`, exact string membership, no case folding, no alias table, no wildcard. The predicate is `held.includes(name)`: exact string membership, no normalisation. ADR-0068's aliases (`user`, `ctx.user`, `os.user`) are aliases of the RECEIVER object, not of capability names, and are the same object by identity, so the identity check admits them; pinned for all four roots. `ec.systemPermissions` is `authz.systemPermissions` (`assemble-execution-context.ts:332`), folded in `resolve-authz-context.ts` from the held set bodies (`foldCatalogSetBodies`) plus, for a configured platform administrator, `ADMIN_FULL_ACCESS_CAPABILITIES.systemPermissions` pushed by name (`:1655`). `/auth/me/permissions` unions `systemPermissions` over `resolvePermissionSetsForContext(execCtx)`, which resolves the names in `context.permissions` — the same names the fold pushed, `admin_full_access` included, and plugin-security seeds that set by spreading the same spec constant (`default-permission-sets.ts:393-403`). So for a platform administrator who is a plain organisation member, the page predicate and the action gate read one list with one content — exactly the divergence the `can('sys_environment','edit')` proxy showed and this predicate closes. A capability granted through a permission set reaches both the same way (set body → fold / union).
  Residuals, neither introduced here and neither a page viewer: (a) `actionPermissionError` bypasses on `ec.isSystem`; a page has no system viewer. (b) An OAuth agent principal (ADR-0090 D10) has `ec.systemPermissions` replaced with its ceiling (`[]` unless `delegatesActions`, then the human's list), while `/auth/me/permissions` for that context unions the agent's restricted sets, which declare no capabilities; when `delegatesActions` is on, the gate reads the human's list and the endpoint answers `[]`. Pages are not rendered by agents, and which list a host binds is the host's (objectui's binding card). (c) Latent, pre-existing on `main`: the security plugin's additive baseline set is applied at set resolution (what `/auth/me/permissions` unions) but `resolveUserAuthzGrants` says it does not fold it (`resolve-authz-context.ts:1209`); the default baseline `member_default` declares no `systemPermissions` (`default-permission-sets.ts:676-1233`, the only explicit list in that file is `organization_admin` at `:487`), so no live divergence today; a deployment whose configured baseline set declares capabilities would publish a name the server gate does not read. Not this PR's to fix; named for the lane (see ③).

**The subject contract — judged right.**
- `EvalContext.systemPermissions?: EvalSystemPermissions` (`ReadonlyArray` of string) and `PermissionBinding.systemPermissions?: EvalSystemPermissions | undefined`, both optional; `celEngine.evaluate` pins `ctx.systemPermissions` into the binding beside `permissions` and does not mount it as a CEL variable, so the function stays the only door — the terms `permissions` already has.
- An existing consumer's typecheck cannot break: both fields are optional additions; `PermissionBinding` literals without the field still satisfy the interface; readers see `undefined`. CI `TypeScript Type Check` (every spec gate, workspace, consumer and source gates) is `success` on this head; the dev also typechecked the subject's consumers and did a reverse TS2322 probe. The published shape is taken verbatim (`GetEffectivePermissionsResponseSchema.systemPermissions: z.array(z.string())`, `protocol.zod.ts`; `ExecutionContext.systemPermissions: z.array(z.string()).optional()`, `execution-context.zod.ts:320`), so the type is the contract's own, not a re-spelling.
- The field has no `toEvalX` door the way `permissions` has `toEvalPermissions`; the shape check (`Array.isArray` and every entry a string) runs inside the predicate per call and refuses loudly. Right for a flat list of names: the door `eval-permissions.ts` argues for exists because an object-permission map has a shape a caller can mis-build; a string list has none to mis-build, and the per-call scan is O(n) over a handful of names, not the schema walk that header warns against.
- **Server-side binders supply no list today — verified: zero `systemPermissions` hits in `packages/objectql/src` non-test source.** `engine.ts` `permissionResolution` (`:6138`) resolves `permissions` only, and only when a predicate calls `can` (`optionVisibilityReadsPermissions` / `readsPermissionPredicate`); `rule-validator.ts` `EvaluateRulesOptions.permissions` (`:399-417`) carries the map only. So `hasCapability` in a validation rule, a CEL `defaultValue`, an option `visibleWhen` or a formula field faults with "carries no capability list" — loud, never a silent false, and the honest answer there (ADR-0137 D2's refusal shape, the same `can` gives when its map is missing). Right that the binders are not wired here: no server predicate calls it, the ruling's consumer is the page surface, and objectql is outside the claim's fence.

**The lint — judged right, oracle verified.** `validateVisibilityPredicates`' unknown-function arm (`validate-visibility-predicates.ts:1128`) asks `firstUnknownFunctionCall`, whose membership set is `buildEnv(...).getDefinitions().functions` — the same constructor `celEngine.compile` and `celEngine.evaluate` use (`unknown-function.ts`, ruling on #13594 refinement 1: the oracle is the engine's registration set, never `CEL_STDLIB_FUNCTIONS`). `registerStdLib` registers `hasCapability` UNCONDITIONALLY, binding or not, so the publish-time verdict and the runtime resolution cannot disagree. The pin on a PAGE component `visibleWhen` with an invented-sibling control (`hasCapabilities` still refused at `error`) is the right pin; the dev's dist-ablation turned it red and back. Is the oracle the same set at every save door? For `os validate` / `os lint` / `os build`: yes — the rule row is `commands: ALL`, `surfaces: CLI_AND_RUNTIME`. For the RUNTIME save door of a `page`: the rule row carries `runtimeTypes: ['view']` (`authoring-rules.ts:1594`), and `runtimeAuthoringRulesFor(type)` filters on exactly that (`runtime-gate.ts:568`), so a `page` written through Studio / REST `/meta` / MCP is judged by none of the visibility-predicate family — the dev's out-of-scope finding is correct as read from the registry, and it is PRE-EXISTING (the row predates this PR; the #7220 comment block above it explains the move onto `view` and even states the rule reads `stack.pages`). This PR changes what the oracle ADMITS, not which door asks it; at the one door that asks for a page (the CLI), the predicate is admitted, and that is the door the pin measures. Judged below as a filing matter, not a defect of this PR.

**The describe — judged truthful and complete for the key it edits.** `PageComponentSchema.visibleWhen` now says: write `current_user.hasCapability('NAME')` with the name the gated action's `requiredPermissions` declares; it answers from the viewer's `systemPermissions`, the list the action gate reads, never a `can(...)` proxy; a host that binds no list makes it fault and a faulting predicate renders the component; ADR-0066 D4: `visibleWhen` hides, `requiredPermissions` refuses. Every sentence is true against the code read above (`actionPermissionError` reads `systemPermissions`; D4 text in `docs/adr/0066-unified-authorization-model.md:71-74`). The sentence was inserted after the `data` root sentences and before the `page:tabs` warning, so the mounted-roots sentence `expression-scope-data-root.pin.test.ts` reads is intact (Test Core green). `content/docs/references/ui/page.mdx` is the only other carrier of this describe (both occurrences regenerated; grep over `packages/spec` and `content/docs` finds no third copy). Left unedited: nav `visible` (`app.zod.ts:369`), `action.visible` (`action.zod.ts:1490`), the `page:tabs` item `visibleWhen` (`component.zod.ts:979`), and the view-form `visibleWhen`s. None of them now says anything untrue — they simply do not name the predicate. `action.visible` should not: an action already declares `requiredPermissions` and naming the predicate there invites a duplicate gate. The nav `visible` is the one worth a follow-up: a navigation entry is a page-node-like surface an author gates on a capability, and if cloud#3036's settings rows are nav entries, that is the describe their author reads. A docs-only follow-up, not a blocker — the predicate works on any surface whose host binds the list, and the describe carries nothing false.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/formula`: `minor` — right. New public function on the standard library (an accept-set widening of every CEL predicate surface), two new exports (`registerCapabilityPredicate`, `EvalSystemPermissions`), a new optional field on two published types. No formula api-surface baseline exists to regenerate (none under `packages/formula`); the stdlib drift pin re-measures and asserts only that receiver-only names stay out of the bare-callable catalog, so a new receiver-only name is absorbed, and `CEL_STDLIB_FUNCTIONS` and `skills/objectstack-formula/SKILL.md` (a Tier H surface) rightly do not move — neither lists `can` either.
- `@objectstack/spec`: `patch` — honest. The one hunk is `.describe()` text on an existing optional key: no schema shape, no new authorable key, no export change; `check:generated` proved only `page.mdx` stale and CI's spec gates are green. The changeset gate's own quantifier (at least one package whose `src/**` moved graded `minor` or above under a `Clause-②: yes` PR, `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` #16361 block) is satisfied by formula; its named residual (a second widened package graded `patch`) does not apply because spec's surface did not widen.
- `@objectstack/core`: rightly untouched. `packages/core/src/evaluator/` and any `subjectPermissions*` file are absent on `origin/main` (`git ls-tree` 0 hits); the evaluator subject is `EvalContext` + `PermissionBinding` in formula, so the card's path was a premise error the dev corrected by measurement. No core changeset is owed.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is present verbatim on both carriers — the changeset body and the PR body — and matches the diff: a widening, nothing narrowed. `can`'s accept set is unchanged (same verbs, same throws); its out-of-vocabulary message gained a pointer sentence, which narrows nothing. `Check Changeset` is `success` on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev deviations, each answered:
1. **File surface moved to `packages/formula`** — accepted; the card's path does not exist (verified above) and the field landed where the subject type lives. The claim's "and `@objectstack/core` if the subject type changes" is the conditional that did not fire.
2. **No lint source change** — accepted; the oracle is the environment (verified in `unknown-function.ts`), so the declared "known-function set" edit was never owed; the pin is the right artifact. The `domain:spec` declarations 6259499592 / 6259504172 named a lint edit that turned out unnecessary — nothing to object to, no lint path is in the diff.
3. **Only the page component describe edited** — accepted with a follow-up: the nav `visible` describe (`app.zod.ts:369`) is the one other page-node surface worth naming the predicate on; docs-only, patch-level, for the lane or `domain:spec` (whose serial note 6259781597 already tracks concurrent describe edits on `page.zod.ts` from #24300 and `app.zod.ts` from PR #24427; whichever lands second merges and keeps both sentences — this head already merged `origin/main` twice).
4. **Trailers** — in order. All five work commits (`c827e8b529` through `e75a7fbd8a`) carry exactly the model-free trailer pair AGENTS.md prescribes — the co-author line with no model name, and the session line naming `session_01AQxxbsMRiqgkrsU3Xd54yE`; the amend was of an unpublished commit; no published history was rewritten.
5. **Detached primary checkout** — a discipline deviation, declared, no damage shown. Switching HEAD on the shared `/home/user/objectstack` checkout is the very motion Prime Directive #11 warns about, even with no file edited there; the cleaner shape is a worktree on a differently named local branch, or `git worktree add --detach` then `git checkout -B` inside the worktree. Note for the lane; not a contract matter. (The primary's HEAD has since been switched again by another session, which is the hazard in evidence.)
6. **cloud#3036 and the objectui card not read** — accepted; the dev's GitHub scope was this repository, the ruling was taken as the card quotes it, and this review did the same by brief.
7. **Seven pushes** — in order; pushing WIP before every long step is the rule, and none was forced.

`open_questions`, each answered:
- **Receiver-only vs bare** — A (receiver-only) is right: it is `can`'s form, the subject is named at the call, the identity check works, and a bare form would either need a second subject binding or answer about nobody; the bare spelling keeps faulting as a call-form fault, so no second dialect exists.
- **Field name `systemPermissions`** — A is right: it is the published response key (`GetEffectivePermissionsResponseSchema`) and the `ExecutionContext` key verbatim, exactly as `permissions` mirrors `objects`; a new vocabulary (`capabilities`) would be a rename an author can get wrong and a second name for one list.
- **Server binders not wired** — A is right for this card: no server-evaluated predicate calls it, the ruling's consumer is the page surface, objectql is outside the claim's fence, and until a binder supplies the list the server answer is a loud fault, not a silent false. When a server predicate needs it, the wiring point is `engine.ts` `permissionResolution` (which would also need a `readsCapabilityPredicate` sibling of `readsPermissionPredicate`, since today the resolver is asked only when `can` is in the source).

`out_of_scope_findings` — the runtime save door and `page`: **verified and it meets a filing gate.** Evidence is contract text, not a hunch: the registry row `validateVisibilityPredicates` declares `surfaces: CLI_AND_RUNTIME, runtimeTypes: ['view']` (`authoring-rules.ts:1588-1596`) while its own comment block states the rule reads `stack.pages`; `runtimeAuthoringRulesFor('page')` therefore excludes the whole visibility-predicate family, so a page `visibleWhen` calling an unregistered function is admitted through Studio / REST `/meta` / MCP and refused only by the CLI. Prime Directive #10 names "a metadata-authoring trap" with its evidence as the filing bar, and a registry row is evidence; a booted repro is not required to file (the card can ask for one). The dev's "carrier: none, noted in Acceptance notes only" under-files it: it should be a card for the lint lane (the family moves as one wall per the #7220 comment, so the fix is `runtimeTypes: ['view', 'page']` on both entries plus the wiring pin). Escalated to the dispatching seat to file; not this PR's defect and not a reason to hold it.

Residual named in ① for the lane, not for this PR: the latent baseline-set divergence between `/auth/me/permissions`' union and `ec.systemPermissions`' fold (`resolve-authz-context.ts:1209`); not live under the default `member_default`, so a measured repro on a configured baseline set should precede a card.
